books.section: Topic 6.9 Responses to Immigration in the Gilded Age

primary_sources: Henry Cabot Lodge, “The Restriction of Immigration,” North American Review, January 1891

stimulus.text:
“Thus it is proved, first, that immigration to this country is increasing, and, second, that it is making its greatest relative increase from races most alien to the body of the American people and from the lowest and most illiterate classes among those races. In other words, it is apparent that, while our immigration is increasing, it is showing at the same time a marked tendency to deteriorate in character.”

Henry Cabot Lodge, “The Restriction of Immigration,” North American Review, January 1891.
stimulus.source_note: Henry Cabot Lodge, “The Restriction of Immigration,” North American Review, vol. 152 (January 1891), p. 32, as reprinted in Publications of the Immigration Restriction League, No. 1 (1894). Public domain; text checked against the Internet Archive scan of the League’s Publications.

stem: According to Lodge, what was happening to immigration?

options.misconception: Claims a fall Lodge never describes.
Claims no change, but Lodge says it was increasing.

options.text: It was coming only from northern and western Europe
options.misconception: Names the old sources Lodge says were being replaced.

options.text: It was increasing, especially from races he called most alien

rationales.A: Lodge says immigration is increasing. A sharp fall is the opposite of his claim.
rationales.B: Lodge says immigration is increasing. Staying the same contradicts his first point.
rationales.C: Lodge says the increase comes from races most alien to Americans, not from northern Europe. The old sources were the earlier wave.
rationales.D: Lodge says it is proved first that immigration is increasing, and second that its greatest relative increase comes from races most alien to the American people. Both parts of his claim are about increase from new sources.
rationales.general:
Take Lodge's two proved points in order.
1. First, Lodge says immigration is increasing.
2. Second, its greatest increase comes from races most alien to Americans.
3. He adds that these are the lowest and most illiterate classes among those races.
4. So immigration was increasing, especially from the groups he called most alien.
Remember: when a writer numbers the proofs, follow the numbers.
